name: RRB Group D
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Level 1 Posts (Group D) Recruitment
conductingBody: Railway Recruitment Boards / RRCs (Ministry of Railways)
approxCandidates: ≈1 crore+ applicants in recent cycles (CEN 08/2024 drew over 1 crore applications; CEN 09/2025 figure approx.)
eligibility: 10th pass or ITI / National Apprenticeship Certificate; 18–33 yrs (relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: Current cycle is CEN 09/2025 for about 22,195 Level-1 posts (Track Maintainer, Pointsman, Assistant, Helper etc.). The CBT was held in August 2026 (3–21 Aug, with a revised schedule reportedly extending to 25 Aug), and the provisional answer key with response sheets was released on 7 Sep 2026 with objections till 15 Sep 2026. The CBT result/PET shortlist was awaited as of the check date. The previous cycle (CEN 08/2024, ~32,438 posts) held its CBT from Nov 2025 to Feb 2026.

pattern.notes: Single CBT, no sectional timing; 1/3 negative marking. Marks normalised across shifts. Minimum qualifying: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. Followed by PET (qualifying), Document Verification and Medical. Science is of Class 10 (CBSE) standard.

trendAnalysis.summary: Group D papers from the 2022 cycle, CEN 08/2024 (Nov 2025–Feb 2026) and CEN 09/2025 (Aug 2026) have been easy-to-moderate. The 25-30-25-20 split (Maths-Reasoning-Science-GA) has been unchanged. Mathematics is direct and formula-based (simplification, percentage, ratio, SI/CI, mensuration, basic trigonometry). Reasoning is the most scoring section: series, coding, analogies, blood relations, syllogism and short puzzles. General Science follows NCERT Class 9–10 with physics numericals (motion, electricity, optics) and biology facts. GA leans on current affairs (sports, schemes, awards) plus static history, polity and geography. Good attempts are typically 75–85.

topics.topic: Square Root, Age, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion

resources.notes: Question papers, provisional answer keys and response sheets are released by the RRBs only for the objection window after each CBT (e.g. 7–15 Sep 2026 for CEN 09/2025) via regional RRB websites such as https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in. There is no permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based shift papers are available from coaching publishers (unofficial).

questions.question: What is the sum of the first 20 natural numbers?
Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: Test for 11: difference of sums of alternate digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11. For 918291: (9 + 8 + 9) − (1 + 2 + 1) = 26 − 4 = 22, a multiple of 11. The others give 21, 20 and 4.

questions.question: Simplify: 125 ÷ 5 of 5 + 3 × 4 − 2
What is the value of 0.25 + 3/8 + 0.125?
What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
The present ages of two brothers are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio will be 3 : 4. What is the present age of the elder brother?
A student scored 342 marks out of 450. What percentage of marks did he score?
What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
12 men can complete a piece of work in 15 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 9 days?
questions.explanation: Total work = 12 × 15 = 180 man-days. Men needed = 180 ÷ 9 = 20.

questions.question: A speed of 54 km/h is equal to how many metres per second?
What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
By selling an article for ₹1,140, a man loses 5%. At what price should he sell it to gain 5%?
If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is the value of a² + b²?
What is the value of sin²30° + cos²60° + tan²45°?
What is the median of the data 7, 3, 9, 12, 5, 10?
questions.explanation: Arranged: 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12. With 6 values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (7 + 9)/2 = 8.

questions.question: Eye : See :: Ear : ?
questions.explanation: The eye is the organ used to see; the ear is the organ used to hear.

questions.question: Select the number that completes the analogy. 25 : 125 :: 36 : ?
questions.explanation: 25 = 5², 125 = 5³. Similarly 36 = 6², so the answer is 6³ = 216.

questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.explanation: Terms are n² + 1 for n = 1 to 5. Next = 6² + 1 = 37 (differences 3, 5, 7, 9, 11).

questions.question: Find the next letter: B, E, I, N, ?
questions.explanation: Positions 2, 5, 9, 14 increase by +3, +4, +5; next is 14 + 6 = 20 = T.

questions.question: Find the next number: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, ?
questions.explanation: These are squares of consecutive primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Next prime is 13, and 13² = 169.

questions.question: If BOOK is coded as 2151511 (using alphabet positions), how is COOK coded?
In a certain code, SMART is written as TRAMS. How will TRAIN be written in that code?
questions.explanation: The word is written in reverse order: TRAIN → NIART.

questions.question: If A means '+', B means '−', C means '×' and D means '÷', what is the value of 18 D 3 C 4 A 5 B 6?
A is the brother of B. C is the father of A. D is the mother of C. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: C is the father of A and hence of B (A and B are siblings). D is C's mother, so D is B's grandmother.

questions.question:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are cats.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Cats ⊂ Dogs ⊂ Birds, so all cats are birds (I). Converting I gives 'Some birds are cats' (II).

questions.question: Arrange the following in a logical sequence: 1. Seed 2. Plant 3. Fruit 4. Flower 5. Sapling
questions.explanation: A seed grows into a sapling, then a plant, which bears flowers that develop into fruits.

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 28 play cricket, 20 play football and 8 play both. How many students play only cricket?
questions.explanation: Only cricket = 28 − 8 = 20.

questions.question: Select the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite of Earth.

questions.question: A, B, C, D and E stand in a row facing north. A is second from the left end. C is to the immediate right of A. B is at the right end. D stands between C and B. Who is at the left end?
questions.explanation: A = 2, C = 3, B = 5, so D = 4 (between C and B). The only remaining place, 1, goes to E.

questions.question: Ravi is facing east. He turns 90° clockwise and then turns 180°. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: East → 90° clockwise → South → 180° → North.

questions.question:
Statement: 'Use our new water purifier to keep your family healthy.' – an advertisement.
Assumptions: I. Clean drinking water helps keep people healthy. II. People want to keep their families healthy.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The advert links purified water to health (I) and appeals to the desire to keep the family healthy (II); both are assumed.

questions.question:
Question: What is Ravi's present age?
Statement I: Ravi is 5 years older than Sunil.
Statement II: Sunil's age is half of Ravi's age.
Which statement(s) are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Both I and II together are needed
Either I or II alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: Neither statement alone gives a value. Together: R = S + 5 and S = R/2 ⇒ R = R/2 + 5 ⇒ R = 10 years.

questions.question: Among P, Q, R, S and T, each has a different height. R is taller than P and S. P is taller than Q. S is taller than P. T is taller than R. Who is the third tallest?
questions.explanation: T > R; R > S; S > P; P > Q. The full order is T > R > S > P > Q, so S is third tallest.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What distance does it cover in this time?
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 2 × 5² = 25 m.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the:
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted on by an external force – the property called inertia.

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 3 m/s?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

questions.question: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. If the speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is the speed of light in glass?
The image formed by a plane mirror is always:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image of the same size, laterally inverted, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.question: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
An electric bulb is rated 100 W, 220 V. What is the resistance of its filament when glowing?
What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), i.e. vibrations per second. Decibel measures sound level, newton force and pascal pressure.

questions.question: An element has atomic number 17. What is its valency?
questions.explanation: Electronic configuration is 2, 8, 7. It needs 1 electron to complete its octet, so its valency is 1 (it is chlorine).

questions.question: Blue litmus paper turns red when it is dipped in:
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red. NaOH solution and lime water are bases; distilled water is neutral.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O. CaSO₄·2H₂O is gypsum.

questions.question: What is the general formula of alkynes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ and alkynes (one triple bond) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, e.g. ethyne C₂H₂.

questions.question: The reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Two reactants combine to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction (it is also an oxidation of magnesium).

questions.question: In plants, the xylem tissue mainly transports:
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves; phloem transports prepared food.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are caused by bacteria.

questions.question: D. Gukesh became the World Chess Champion in December 2024 by defeating which player in the title match?
questions.explanation: Gukesh beat China's Ding Liren 7.5–6.5 in Singapore in December 2024 to become the youngest undisputed world champion.

questions.question: In August 2023, India's Chandrayaan-3 mission made a soft landing in which region of the Moon?
questions.explanation: On 23 August 2023 the Vikram lander touched down near the south pole of the Moon, making India the first country to land in that region.

questions.question: The new Parliament building of India in New Delhi was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: The new Parliament building was inaugurated on 28 May 2023.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji gave the call 'Do or Die' at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, in August 1942.

questions.question: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.explanation: The massacre took place at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 14 is equality before law, 21 is right to life and 32 is constitutional remedies.

questions.question: The Sundarbans delta is formed mainly by which rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans lie in the Ganga–Brahmaputra (–Meghna) delta in West Bengal and Bangladesh.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in Assam.

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced which body in January 2015?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (1950).

questions.question: Pongal is a harvest festival mainly celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in mid-January.

questions.question: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) is the autobiography of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, written with Arun Tiwari.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme?
questions.explanation: Dr Vikram Sarabhai founded INCOSPAR (1962) which became ISRO; he is called the father of India's space programme.
